title: POC scoping: hosted vs dedicated vs private - BrightCare Health
next_steps: Send detailed pricing for Hosted/Dedicated/Private and reserved capacity options
Share SOC2/ISO and network architecture security pack
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run on Hosted environment using customer sample dataset (week of 2026-12-27)
Prepare Dedicated capacity sizing proposal and quotes
Provide integration checklist for SSO/KMS and observability hooks
action_items: Jared Kim: Send pricing and reserved capacity options (2026-12-22)
Lina Patel: Draft benchmark plan and script, include KV cache and burst scenarios (2026-12-23)
Ethan Liu: Share sample traffic traces and redaction rules (2026-12-22)
Priya Menon: Send security requirements and regulatory constraints (2026-12-22)
summary: POC scoping call to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for BrightCare Health. Discussed success criteria (latency SLOs, throughput, cost targets, security approvals), workload sizing, benchmark plan and timelines. Agreed to run initial hosted benchmark next week, then size Dedicated if needed; Private considered only if regulatory blockers persist. Action items assigned for pricing, benchmark scripts, and customer artifacts.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private decision criteria
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Lina Patel (Redwood SE), Sara Gomez (BrightCare CTO), Ethan Liu (BrightCare Infra Lead), Priya Menon (BrightCare Security)

[00:00] Jared Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call, i'm Jared from Redwood, lina is our SE, and we got the BrightCare folks on. Sara, Ethan, Priya, can you confirm?
[00:06] Sara Gomez: Yep this is Sara, hi.
[00:07] Ethan Liu: Ethan here.
[00:08] Priya Menon: Priya on security. Thanks for setting up.
[00:12] Jared Kim: Awesome. Quick agenda: scoping the POC \u0014 success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks, and then the big decision: hosted vs dedicated vs private. We'll cover timelines and next steps. Sound good?
[00:18] Sara Gomez: Sounds great. We're mainly trying to validate latency and cost with our real traffic, plus security must-haves.
[00:23] Lina Patel: Perfect. maybe i'll start with a high-level of our deployment modes and when customers typically pick each, then we'll get into specifics.

[02:05] Lina Patel: So hosted = fastest to test, we run inference on Redwood managed infra, you get immediate access, streaming, function calling, etc. Dedicated = reserved GPU pools for your tenant, predictable throughput and SLA. Private = VPC/private control plane or on-prem where we can hand over network boundaries. Common tradeoffs: cost predictability and throughput favor Dedicated, data residency and strict compliance sometimes push to Private. Hosted usually best for quick benchmarks.

[03:12] Ethan Liu: For us, two constraints: we have PHI in transcripts so data residency and encryption are top. Also bursty QPS \u0014 sorting peak around 120 qps for short windows, avg around 12 qps. Latency goal is p95 under 600ms for a 512-token response. Cost target, we don't have an exact number but we'd like to estimate token cost and total monthly.

[04:00] Priya Menon: On PHI, we need SOC2, logs/audit trail, and KMS integration. If hosted cannot meet our encryption-in-transit and at-rest with customer-managed keys, private may be required. Does Redwood support HSM-backed keys?
[04:18] Lina Patel: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports KMS for encryption but for customer-managed HSM we typically recommend Private. I should note, some customers use hosted with token-level redaction and then move to dedicated once compliance sign-offs are done. There's a gradation.

[05:02] Jared Kim: For the POC, typical approach: run an initial hosted benchmark using a sample of your traffic, measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, and cost. If metrics meet your success criteria we can continue on hosted or size Dedicated for predictable latency and cost cap. Private is reserved for hard compliance blocks.

[05:30] Sara Gomez: That's the path i was picturing. We want to agree success criteria up front. I'll propose: 1) p95 latency < 600ms for 512 tokens, 2) throughput sustain at 100 qps for 2-minute bursts, 3) cost no more than X \u0014 we need Redwood to help estimate, 4) security checklist satisfied (SOC2, KMS, SSO).

[06:05] Lina Patel: Works. For cost estimate we need input: average tokens per request, prompt vs generation split, embedding usage if any, and monthly volume.

[06:20] Ethan Liu: Average tokens per request is ~420 (prompt + generation), generation portion ~300 tokens. We do embeddings intermittently for search, about 100k embeddings/month. Monthly inference tokens roughly 180M input + 120M output = 300M tokens.

[07:00] Jared Kim: Great, that gives us a starting point. Lina, we can use their 300M tokens to roughly model both hosted and dedicated costs, and then include batching/kv cache effects.

[07:20] Lina Patel: Quick note on KV cache \u0014 since you have many multi-turn sessions we can leverage prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated prompt tokens. That will reduce cost significantly for recurring sessions. But caching effectiveness depends on session patterns. Ethan, can you share sample session traces?

[07:40] Ethan Liu: I'll share them after the call. We do spend a lot on repeated system prompts across sessions so caching could be huge.

[08:12] Priya Menon: Another question: audit logs and retention. We need full request/response logs for 90 days and ability to redact PII. Is that available?

[08:22] Lina Patel: Yes, audit logs and configurable retention are supported. Automatic PII redaction we can include in pipeline but if you need guaranteed removal we often implement callback hooks with your side processing or Private deployment where logs never leave your VPC.

[09:00] Sara Gomez: Okay, timeline. How long to get a hosted benchmark up and running? We want numbers next week ideally.

[09:10] Jared Kim: We can run a basic hosted benchmark within 48-72 hours if we get sample dataset and traffic traces today. For a production-like run with KV caching and burst patterns, two steps: quick run and a larger 2-hour run that simulates bursts.

[09:30] Lina Patel: i'll prepare a benchmark script that replays traffic, includes multi-turn scenarios, and measures p50/p95/p99 and token counts. We'll also capture latencies with and without batching.

[10:12] Ethan Liu: Do you need environment access or can we just give you traces?

[10:18] Lina Patel: Traces + redaction rules is enough for hosted benchmark. For Dedicated we'd do a sizing exercise based on results.

[11:05] Priya Menon: On encryption: can hosted support customer-managed keys for at-rest? We need to make sure keys are not accessible by third parties.

[11:14] Lina Patel: Hosted supports provider-managed encryption; customer-managed KMS is possible for Dedicated and Private. Some hosted customers use envelope encryption workflows where sensitive fields are encrypted client-side before sending. We can go through options in the security pack.

[12:00] Sara Gomez: So far sounds like plan: hosted benchmark first, if we hit latency/cost goals then maybe hosted or Dedicated depending on predictability needs. If security blocks then move to Private. Can you walk through the decision criteria you use when recommending Dedicated vs Private?

[12:20] Lina Patel: Sure. Decision criteria matrix - summarizing verbally: 
- Choose Hosted if: want fastest time-to-value, no strict KMS/HSM or on-prem requirement, and acceptable to use managed infra; good for evaluation and many production cases.
- Choose Dedicated if: you need predictable throughput, SLA-backed latency/uptime, reserved capacity for burst avoidance, and customer-managed KMS is required but can be integrated in Dedicated or Private. Also when cost predictability/pooling is important.
- Choose Private if: regulatory or contractual obligations require VPC-only, air-gapped or on-prem, or you need HSM-backed keys that can't be supported in hosted model. Also customers with network egress restrictions.

[13:25] Jared Kim: I'll add: Dedicated often reduces unit cost at scale because you're reserving capacity and can achieve better batching and optimized kernels for your model. Private is the most complex to deploy and takes longer.

[14:00] Ethan Liu: What's the typical lead time for Dedicated? We're looking at a Q1 production target.

[14:08] Lina Patel: Depends on commit size. If you go Dedicated with reserved capacity, deployment is typically 3-6 weeks \u2014 includes sizing, procurement, and onboarding. Private/VPC on-prem can be 8-12 weeks depending on your infra and approvals. Hosted benchmark can be immediate.

[15:00] Sara Gomez: For our compliance team, they will push for Private if keys must be HSM and logs cannot leave environment. Priya, is that current expectation?

[15:07] Priya Menon: We're not yet fixed; initial posture is we'd prefer customer-managed HSM for keys for PHI handling. If Redwood can show equivalent control in Dedicated with HSM integration, we can consider that. If not, Private becomes necessary. We need documentation.

[15:35] Lina Patel: We'll attach the SOC2/ISO pack and a KMS integration doc. For Dedicated we do have customers integrating with external HSMs via a supported flow; i'll document the exact architecture.

[16:10] Jared Kim: On benchmarks: we also want to simulate KV cache hit rates. If your traffic has 40-60% repeat prefixes, effective token cost can drop. Lina, can we include cache-on and cache-off runs?

[16:22] Lina Patel: Absolutely. We'll run three permutations in the benchmark script: cold (no cache), warm (simulated 50% cache hits), and burst (peak QPS replay). We'll capture CPU/GPU utilization, token throughput, and request latencies.

[17:05] Ethan Liu: Any caveats about model selection? We currently are evaluating a 13B open model vs a 70B quantized variant. Which would be better for Dedicated?

[17:18] Lina Patel: For latency and cost, quantized 70B on optimized kernels can be similar latency to 13B but higher memory needs. Dedicated allows you to pick the instance type and quantization profile. We'll include a model comparison in the benchmark. If you can tell us exact model checkpoints we can compile a performance profile.

[18:00] Sara Gomez: We'll share model names and checkpoints after the call.

[18:20] Priya Menon: A couple of procurement questions: SOC2 Type II reports, penetration test artifacts, and data flow diagrams \u2014 can you provide those?

[18:28] Jared Kim: Yes, we'll include SOC2 and penetration test summaries. Data flow diagrams we'll sketch for hosted/dedicated/private so your procurement team can review.

[19:12] Lina Patel: Also, for network, if you go Dedicated in a cloud region, we support private peering and direct connect options. For Private we run inside your VPC or on-prem package. We'll list the network requirements and port lists in the security pack.

[20:05] Ethan Liu: On observability, we need token-level cost, per-route latency, and tracing. Is the Redwood console accessible in Dedicated/Private?

[20:15] Lina Patel: Yes, Redwood Console works across all modes but data available depends on deployment. Dedicated gets the same dashboard; Private can have control-plane telemetry forwarded to your SIEM or a self-hosted console. We can set RBAC and SSO for your team.

[21:00] Sara Gomez: What about canary rollouts and automatic fallback if a model degrades? We need resiliency.

[21:10] Jared Kim: We support rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. For example, if a model's quality drops or latency increases beyond a threshold, we can failover to a cheaper or older checkpoint. We'll show examples in the follow-up deck.

[22:05] Priya Menon: Let's nail success criteria in writing so the POC is unambiguous. I'll suggest: p95 < 600ms for 512 tokens, p99 < 1.2s, sustain 100 qps for bursts, overall monthly token cost within 20% of Redwood estimate, audit/logging and KMS options validated.

[22:30] Jared Kim: Agreed. We'll put that in the POC doc. Lina will own the benchmark and metrics.

[23:05] Lina Patel: I'll also produce an acceptance checklist: test plan, benchmark script, performance thresholds, security checklist (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and integration checklist for observability.

[24:00] Ethan Liu: If hosted benchmark meets criteria, is it common to run production on hosted or do companies typically shift to Dedicated for cost predictability?

[24:12] Lina Patel: Many start hosted in production for small volumes, then shift to Dedicated as they scale and want guaranteed capacity and lower unit cost. Some stay hosted if traffic patterns are smooth and compliance is satisfied.

[25:00] Sara Gomez: Good. Procurement will also need estimated monthly cost delta between hosted and Dedicated with reserved capacity; can you provide a model?

[25:08] Jared Kim: We'll produce a cost model with assumptions: batching efficiency, cache hit rate, and quantization. That will show per-token unit cost for hosted and reserved tiers.

[26:00] Priya Menon: One more security note: we require separation of logs by tenant, and ability to confirm no other tenants can access our raw payloads. How is multi-tenancy handled?

[26:15] Lina Patel: We provide tenant isolation at the control plane. In Hosted we logically isolate workloads and encrypt at-rest; Dedicated provides stronger isolation by single-tenant infra. Private gives you full control. We'll include an architecture note for tenant isolation.

[27:00] Ethan Liu: Benchmarks \u2014 what metrics will you collect besides latency and TPS?

[27:06] Lina Patel: We'll collect token counts, GPU utilization, memory usage, queue times, batch sizes, KV cache hit rates, and error rates. We'll also capture end-to-end latencies including network time from client to Redwood endpoint.

[28:00] Sara Gomez: Ok timeline recap \u2014 can we do the hosted benchmark next week? We want results by 2026-12-29.

[28:10] Jared Kim: Yes. Action plan: BrightCare shares traces and sample dataset by 2026-12-22. Lina drafts benchmark script by 2026-12-23. Hosted 2-hour benchmark scheduled week of 2026-12-27. Results and cost model by 2026-12-29. Does that align?

[28:30] Ethan Liu: That works from our side.

[29:05] Priya Menon: We'll also start internal compliance review in parallel. If we see any blockers we'll escalate and consider Private.

[30:00] Jared Kim: Cool. A few clarifying Qs: Ethan, you said bursts ~120 qps \u2014 is that sustained by endpoint or distributed across multiple endpoints?

[30:10] Ethan Liu: That's aggregate across our front-end instances hitting the same model endpoint. We can shard but want the endpoint to handle aggregates.

[31:00] Lina Patel: We'll simulate aggregate load in the benchmark. Also, we'll test both single big request patterns and many concurrent small requests to surface queueing behaviors.

[32:05] Sara Gomez: On model upgrades, how do rollouts affect P95? We need safe rollout plan.

[32:15] Jared Kim: We recommend canary deploys with traffic steering and automatic metrics-based rollbacks. We'll provide standard SLO-based rollback thresholds.

[33:10] Priya Menon: Data residency \u2014 our data must not transit through certain regions. Can Redwood route requests to specific regions?

[33:20] Lina Patel: Yes, smart routing can pin to regions or tiers. For Hosted we'll ensure region selection; Dedicated and Private provide more control. We'll document region compliance options.

[34:05] Ethan Liu: For Dedicated sizing, besides QPS, what other factors are key?

[34:15] Lina Patel: Model size, sequence length, batchability, and KV cache effectiveness. Also expected concurrency and acceptable queueing. We'll recommend instance types and reserved counts once we have benchmark numbers.

[35:00] Sara Gomez: What's the rollback if the Dedicated pool gets overloaded?

[35:06] Jared Kim: We have autoscale and fallback to hosted spare capacity or lower-cost checkpoints depending on your policy. For Dedicated customers we can configure burst capacity to spillover to hosted under strict conditions. We'll include options in the proposal.

[36:10] Priya Menon: On certs and pen tests \u2014 can you provide the latest reports under NDA?

[36:18] Jared Kim: Yes we can share under NDA. We'll include those in the security pack.

[37:05] Lina Patel: Quick note about accuracy/regression monitoring: Redwood Optimize can hook into your evals and flag regressions against baseline prompts. We'll include that as an optional add-on.

[38:00] Ethan Liu: Good, we'll want alerts on prompt drift and quality regressions.

[39:05] Sara Gomez: Any blockers for starting the hosted benchmark next week?

[39:12] Lina Patel: Nothing from our side if we get the artifacts and access to any sample credentials for rate-limiting parameters.

[40:00] Ethan Liu: We'll share traces and a small redacted dataset. Expect that by 12/22.

[41:05] Priya Menon: We'll also share our security questionnaire so you can fill the vendor responses.

[42:00] Jared Kim: Great. We'll prepare: pricing sheet, SOC2/ISO pack, KMS/HSM integration doc, benchmark script, cost model, and a decision matrix for hosted/dedicated/private.

[42:30] Lina Patel: I'll reach out with the benchmark template and required fields for traces.

[43:00] Sara Gomez: Can you include estimate for time to migrate from hosted to Dedicated if we decide after POC?

[43:08] Jared Kim: We'll include an estimated timeline: typically 3-6 weeks for Dedicated onboarding. We'll note dependencies like procurement and signed commitment.

[44:05] Ethan Liu: For the benchmark, can you simulate KV cache with our prefix patterns or do we need to annotate traces?

[44:12] Lina Patel: Annotated traces help. If not possible we'll infer common prefixes but annotated is preferred for fidelity.

[45:00] Priya Menon: Any SLA details for Dedicated?

[45:05] Jared Kim: We'll include SLA targets in the Dedicated proposal \u2014 uptime, latency targets, and credits for violations.

[46:10] Sara Gomez: Let's summarize action items and next steps.

[46:18] Jared Kim: Action items recap: Jared to send pricing and security pack by 12/22; Lina to share benchmark script by 12/23 and run hosted benchmark week of 12/27; BrightCare to share traces and redaction rules by 12/22; Priya to start compliance review and share questionnaire.

[47:00] Ethan Liu: Sounds good. We'll be ready to collaborate.

[48:05] Priya Menon: One last quick question \u2014 do you have references of healthcare customers who did similar transitions?

[48:12] Lina Patel: Yes we do; we'll include anonymized case studies showing Dedicated migrations and compliance patterns.

[49:00] Sara Gomez: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll wait for your docs and the benchmark plan.

[49:10] Jared Kim: Thanks all \u2014 we'll follow up with the POC doc and calendar invites.

[54:00] Meeting end.

Notes/Artifacts referenced: POC benchmark script (link to be shared), SOC2/ISO pack (attached), pricing spreadsheet (to be shared), sample dataset and traces (customer to provide).

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors on acronyms (VPC/V P C, KV cache sometimes transcribed as K V cache), filler words and overlaps present.
